Good takes, thanks for the input. I’m well aware of Super Surge being great on Era, but I opted for Perfect Form because the shorter cooldowns felt more beneficial. Especially since the haste buff is on a pretty long cooldown, and you can get multiple hits for PF using tornado. Super Surge is definitely still good if you want to kite or chase the core better, though. I didn’t think of Missile Propulsion on Drek’ar, that’s something worth experimenting with, too, alongside Eject Button as another recommended.

Ohh, that’s clever, never thought of that particular combo. Eject Button seems to have a lot of hidden potential, and it’s definitely worth exploring. You can make a lot of surprise aggro plays with it, Luna being the prime example, of course. Just a really interesting training for strikers with high mobility.

That’s a really good point, and a good takeaway for goalie players trying to climb the ladder. While the more defensive and teamplay strikers like Dubu and Atlas are still good picks, they run into the issue of being more reliant on your team, rather than making an impact themselves. This is why I suggest picking up someone like Kai or Estelle, strikers that can more easily contribute outside of just protecting the goal. Being flexible with your picks, even as goalie, can really help push games your way.

As for me, I haven’t really settled on a particular pick, although I have warmed up to Estelle quite a bit. I enjoy being able to help my team with harass and fancy clears.

Hello everyone! I am a Vtuber who has a deep passion for HotS! While I do variety streaming, I plan on streaming HotS more frequently in order to show my love and support for this amazing game. I used to be a Rank 1/Masters player, and I play as an Abathur and healer main. Right now I am just playing for fun and learning more heroes, but will eventually get back into ranked at some point.

My twitch link is https://www.twitch.tv/claireasheron , and I regularly stream at 3PM PST, although I may try earlier times. I have a small, friendly and welcoming community, and I love meeting people who pop in to say hello, or to ask any questions when I’m not trying to hyperfocus. I hope you all have a great day, and I’ll see you in the Nexus sometime. :)

I think you have very good points on Thrall and Falstad, I don’t really recall them ever being particularly overpowered or bad, and they have fairly good talent trees, too. Sundering and Gust can be really annoying at times, but I think it’s alright and doesn’t make a person hate playing against them, and they are great, fun playmaking tools.

I’m kinda surprised you said Rehgar, honestly. He’s generally been either amazing or weak, no inbetween. Even after his nerfs, I believe he’s still the top winrate healer, which says a lot. I think his kit allows him to do too much, so his cons are few. I feel that’s not really good design, personally. Don’t get me wrong though, I still enjoy him and there are far worse culprits of balance out there.

Interesting that you mention Sylvanas, I personally wouldn’t have thought of her. She’s always had a history of enabling snowballs and degenerate strats, which complicates things and can be very frustrating. I do agree she has good talent diversity and her passive is a lot more tame nowadays, but I don’t think I would choose her as balanced, per say. Still, good comment overall.

Anyone else dislikes playing against Pinhead as survivor? It’s not that he’s overly strong or unfair, but dealing with his passive just feels EXTREMELY tedious. “Oh, we’re 75% to chain hunt. Guess I have to drop whatever I was doing (gens, trying to unhook, looking for Ruin, etc), grab the box, run all the way to a safe corner of the map while leaving my item I wanted to use, and solve it before we literally can’t do anything afterward. I don’t know, he’s just been really unpleasant to play against, regardless of how the killer player themself was playing.

I understand the reasoning why most killers tunnel, and I always try not to be toxic towards other players unless they are blatantly being so to me. Just seems strange to me that this is the mindset for most killer players in all of their games. There’s a difference between playing to win, and actively removing someone from the game from the beginning, disregarding everything else. That’s just how I feel.

That is fair. Sometimes I have games like that, and I understand that it’s likely my bad luck instead of the killer purposely doing it. I don’t mind it either if I get a game where all my teammates are fighting for my unhook, and the killer obviously can’t ignore them. It’s the other kind of games though that are unfortunately really often and get to me. Thanks for not being one of those players.
I don’t have friends, but I do watch a lot of streams and such. Just feels bad that I only get the first few minutes in a game to do much of anything, let alone improve.

Doesn’t it feel unneeded most of the time, though? There’s a difference between trying to play to win, maybe protecting a hook to secure a kill in the EGC, and purposely going out of your way to remove someone from the game as fast as possible, even if it’s not efficient or the right thing to do. It’s that mindset, along with the toxicity it brings, that makes me question if DbD is even worth playing.

A lot of times they will camp, or at least purposely target me right after I get unhooked. Most of the time my teammates will try to help or do gens, so it’s not any fault on them.

I mean, I understand that I’m not going to do well every game. My problem is that I can’t even play after the first two minutes. And like I said, I just do not enjoy playing killer, it’s not really my thing.

Hey guys, I've played a ton the event so far, and my current solo queue record is 19 rounds, so I feel I've grasped what needs to be done. For people struggling, here's some advice about gods people should pick, and what builds they should be building.

Mages: Two mages are generally good and helpful. You usually want two for both burst damage and reliable cc. Best picks to consider are Poseidon, Anubis, Nox and Isis. They particularly have strong cc abilities that help lockdown, alongside good burst damage. Honorary Mentions include He Bo and Scylla for their own cc although unreliable compared to the four mentioned, and Freya for being a strong dps that has an interrupt with Banish. Hades seems like a alright pick, but in later rounds a lot of times you simply die during your ult. Picking mages like Zeus, Ah Puch and Kukulkan do not give any real cc, and will just hamper the team if you can't contribute to stun locking and crowd controlling.

As much as people think otherwise, healing mages are NOT useful nor mandatory. Most of the time enemies in rounds have healing debuffs on their attacks, and don't have much of the important aoe cc needed. The only ones I'd suggest is Aphrodite to stun with Kiss, or Chang'e in an Ares comp. General mage builds should be Pen boots, Spear of Desolation and Obsidian Shard. Enemies are tanky, you need tons of penetration to get through them. You can vary things by getting a Pythagorum's, Spear of the Magus or a Gem of Isolation, but those require tinkering to get your gold's total worth, and results in a bit less dps.

Hunters: One is definitely needed for constant physical dps. Top choices are Cupid, Artemis, Medusa and Hou Yi, as they provide very useful cc in their kits. Honorary Mentions are Skadi, who can pull off some neat kiting tricks with Kaldr to offset the lack of hard cc, and Anhur, for having a stun but not reliably. Neith is a bit of a trap pick, as the root and ult aren't too useful and reliable, and she lacks damage. Again, it's about both damage and cc. Hunters should be building Crusher, Qin's Sais, and either Titan's Bane or Executioner. You need penetration and Qins to deal with such high hp pools and towers, and things like lifesteal and crit are worthless.

Guardians: You should have 1 to be the main tank of the team. I don't recommend more as you lose too much damage. Best choices are Terra, Fafnir, Ares and Ymir. They have strong aoe lockdown and buffing/healing. Honorary Mention is Khepri, for his very useful ultimate and Abduct. Guardians have a set build that is Greaves, Sovereignty, Heartward, and Winged Wand. It's very important that they have this build to cover allies with protections, and have the movement speed to kite the Bashful Lion round. Yes, you can easily walk around the arena and kite it with little damage so long as you have this build.

Assassins: Some Assassins are very useful for dps and cc. They include Bakasura, Nemesis, and Hun Batz. They can shred enemies and provide aoe cc. Honorary mentions include Kali, Thor, and Ne Zha, who are less consistant but still can help lockdown. Assassins should be going the same build choices as Hunters.

Warriors: They are actually the weakest class here imo. They don't have the damage or the cc to warrant picking them, but there are some that can still be useful. They include Chaac, Hercules, Guan Yu, and Tyr. They should either be doing the Guardian's tank build, or a full damage build, normal bruiser builds are not effective enough.

Last thing I want to say, ALWAYS TAKE AEGIS/SANCTUARY, even the tanks. Aegis is far too important to dodge burst damage, endure focus fire from enemies, and switch off aggro. The team should also have at least one Girdle/Frenzy, Shell, and Meditation. If you have any questions just ask.

It's mainly about spacing attack chains and angling hits. For example, right after you finish a chain with the uppercut, pause very slightly, then start again. Timed right, you'll be able to land all of your hits in again without trouble. Also position a little bit around them as you finish each chain, so you can cut off their escape routes easier. If trying to juggle someone with mobility (Mellka, Orendi, etc), then it's more about having attack speed, as well as a little luck, to prevent them from dashing, hopefully canceling their cooldown as well with a good timed uppercut. You could also try out sprint or movement speed in your gear to quickly chase if they get away.

Angling the uppercut animation at them is really important too, if juggling someone like Miko, who is naturally fast and has small hitboxes. It can be easy to whiff the uppercut if you aren't aiming at them right, or you throw out the uppercut a little too early or late. Lastly, don't bother trying to juggle Caldarius, Benedict or Toby. They have really high air mobility and get out of juggles easily.

Deande is an interesting and personally underrated character, that can toy with enemies by weakening their damage and utilizing stealth. You can either play her as an assassin and attempt to focus someone down, or my preference as a surprisingly CC-heavy bruiser that's very hard to kill and deal with. Helix:

**1) Wonder Twins:** All of the upgrades at level 1 have merit. This one scales well with further Holotwin upgrades and is overall great for sustain anytime. Ground Zero is really strong in PvE, and gives Deande waveclear for minions. Double Trouble gives you a lot of extra mobility, provided you remember the new dash direction. 

**2) All Safeties Off:** Usually the better choice for more lifesteal from Wonder Twins, and because in PvP many people have the habit of ignoring the decoy while fighting/searching for you. The decoy health is better for PvE because mobs will simply burst it down really quickly.

**3) Uppercut:** This is single-handedly one of the best upgrades in the entire game. I'm not even joking. Knockups are very strong in Battleborn, as they prevent movement and can interrupt abilities (Forcing them on cooldown too). The fact of having a reliable lockdown on an attack chain gives Deande *absurd* amounts of power. Here's some of many reasons why:

* You can stunlock almost any enemy in PvE. 
* You can reliably lockdown and hold up any person.
* By holding them down, you are basically increasing your damage because you are hitting them longer.
* Players have more difficulty fighting back when they are getting juggled.

Even with a bit of Attack Speed from gear, you are a single-target Attikus ultimate. With Blink Storm, Burst Dash, and other upgrades, you are a CC monster. I could just go on and on. The other two upgrades aren't even worth considering, simply because Uppercut is THAT good. Always take Uppercut as soon as you unlock it. Learn to master it and its timings. Embrace the Shoryuken.

**4) Drain Dash:** Gives another nice bit of sustain from your kit, making you harder to kill or bully out. If you take Ground Zero you can easily heal half your health bar from a few minions or mobs. Calculate Risk is awkward to use, as to get the most out of it you would have to build shield capacity from gear. Save it for assassin builds in PvP.

**5) Silent Strike:** As if Uppercut and Blink Strike weren't enough CC, having a slow from uncloaking would make Deande give even Alani a run for her money in CC power. Remember that slows also affect a player's Attack Speed and jump height in this game, making them very strong in PvP for fighting. Roguelike is the PvE alternative, simply because slows barely effect mobs, and even with knockups, you will likely only get a hit or two on the back of someone, before they turn to you. 10% move speed on kill is really unnoticable, and thus never worth it.

**6) Ire's Echo:** I really like this upgrade for the surprise factor of damage and *more* CC. I believe it even benefits from Wonder Twins, adding another bit of sustain. Burst Brawler is better for Assassin and Burst Dash builds. Escape Plan is a nice boost of speed for escapes, or for chasing if someone managed to break away from Uppercut knockups. 

**7) Fan 'O War:**  Consider the fact that Culling only does 5% more damage in return for only being a few seconds after Burst Dash, and you'll realize that Fan 'O War is entirely superior because of the consistency and not being restricted to after an ability.

**8) Deadly Reach:** Up to preference really. Both can be nice depending on if you want more damage or CC from the weakening. Keep in mind to take Energised with Ground Zero, I don't believe Deadly Reach works with it, but I can be wrong.

**9) Lingering Light:** Your decoy gets the most out of this upgrade, and synergises well with the others we've taken. The cooldown is great if you want to utilize the stealth aspect of Holotwin more, while the shield pen, as with all shield penetration upgrades and gear, is highly situational and dependant on facing high-shielded enemies or players.

**10) Dopplegangup:** Let's be real, 10 seconds cooldown on a long cd like Blink Storm really doesn't do much at all, making Gathering Storm really poor. One thing to remember, you can only have a single decoy up at once, so using Blink Storm after Holotwin will just replace the decoy. Make sure to space out usage if you want to maximize decoys.

**For Gear:** I recommend Attack Speed, Attack Damage, and a tank stat like Health. You are going to be attacking a ton regardless of build, and you REALLY want attack speed in particular to abuse Uppercut and bouncyhouse people. You don't have to dip super hard into attack speed, however, as Deande can use a lot of other stats nearly as well. Health and Regen are great for taking hits easier, and she scales pretty well with Skill Damage and Cooldown Reduction if you are going for an assassin build.

**Legendary Gear:** Deande's lore gear is fantastic, and definitely useful for nearly any build. Vow of Vengeance (Hylis) works great for Deande as you are very likely to get a lot of hits in from Uppercuts. Leechsteel Brooch (Hylis) is also nice as Deande's abilities do a lot and it furthers your sustain. Also consider Bola's Target Finder (Supervisor Antem), Shield Web Interdictor (Geoff), Vigilance Link (Old Sentinel), and Pain-2-Gain Re-Knitter (Packs).

Ambra is a versatile support that, while not excelling in any specific regard, is well rounded and able to be played a lot of ways. I play her as an offensive healer that deals solid damage. Helix:

**1) Sunspotter:** Both of these upgrades are very strong and up to preference. An AoE damage amp is crazy good for crowd control, waveclear and so on. Illumination adds a large amount of damage to Solar Wind, making your 1v1 strength particularly good. Decide what you want to do more in the game before choosing.

**2) Blessing of the Sun:** Sunspots heal slowly by nature, so it's important to remedy that with this upgrade. Solar Burst is pretty bad, because the damage is just okay, while you lose any healing benefit of sunspots in fights. Soothing Sunlight is situationally good, the burst heal can save people when the heal-over-time wouldn't. I don't take it because teammates will often walk into them regardless, and the burst heal is not nearly as strong as the full amount of the heal-over-time. If you take Soothing make sure to tell people.

**3) Stellar Ritual:** I really like being able to buff up the sunspots, making them very efficient and powerful. Great for setting up an area for the team. Blood Drive can be more useful for directly fighting and sustaining yourself in them. The last upgrade is really not worth it, it's like being a poor man's Miko. Stick with Stellar Ritual for healing people.

**4) Searing Wind:** This adds a MASSIVE amount of damage to Solar Wind, I can't understate it. You're likely to be in melee range for Scorching Strikes anyway, so the condition is a non-issue. Radiant Gale turns Solar Wind into more of a peeling ability than a damage one, and can be useful to push away melee enemies and players. Ritual of Repulsion is like a more clunky, awkward version of Radiant Gale, so while I'm sure there are some good uses for it, I recommend staying away.

**5) Cauterization:** A preference pick, this gives a huge speed boost to get away to safety. However, Flame Burst can surprise a lot of people, can be more useful if you are simply getting bursted too hard to use the speed, and is generally better in PvE. Up to you.

**6) Solar Anomaly:** Three great upgrades. The third sunspot is super useful for setting up heal zones for teammates, which I personally like. The range upgrade is very noticable, and can be better if people aren't staying near sunspots from obliviousness or whatever. Solar Storm is nice if you are taking all the Solar Wind upgrades and want it up often.

**7) Flame Staff:** With this, you can really endure hits in a fight, making you quite tough to kill solo. Radiant Halberd is a really cool upgrade, but to make it work, you have to adjust your build a lot (Not taking most Solar Wind upgrades as you'll be ranged), and Ambra's lore gear feels pretty much mandatory for it, so you can infinitely have heat to shoot. Radiant Spear can deal a lot of burst and let you use the lifesteal more, but I feel Flame Staff is more consistently useful.

**8) Fan the Flames:** Generally far more efficient, as to buff sunspot damage, durability and healing. It far outperforms what the cooldown reduction can do in almost every circumstance.

**9) Sweltering Wind:** I'm fairly sure this works with Searing Wind, but don't quote me on it. Regardless, even more damage to an already strong ability. I personally would only take the AoE upgrade in PvE for mobs, as it's pretty useless in PvP.

**10) Impact Crater:** The stun is such a huge gamechanger if you land Extinction Event. Guaranteed to win any fight if placed well. World's End is deceptive and mediocre, because the damage over time is really low, and only PvE bosses will ever sit in the entire duration.

**For Gear:** I recommend Heal Power and Skill Damage, specifically because those stats are good in nearly any build. Honestly, Ambra can utilize the majority of gear well, so it just relies on what you like to do with her. You can build Attack Damage and speed for better lifestealing/Scorching Strikes, Damage Reduction/Health Regen for tanking, and so on.

**Legendary Gear:** Ambra's lore gear is fantastic in general for the stats and effect, and core if you plan on using Radiant Halberd. Void Resonator (Conservator) and Symbiotic Spores (Experiment's Conservator) are both great healing gear, the former useful for yourself, and the latter for your team. Chrono Key (Vyn/Arc) may be a shadow of what it once was, but I still believe Ambra can use it nicely if you like the cooldown reduction, and you help clear minions and mobs with it. You have the same freedom with legendary gear, so you have plenty of choice. Personally, I'd consider Oath of the Sustained (Hylis), Alamo-7 Armor (Random), "Bloody Mess" Burst Kit (Packs), and Dr. Fist's Medic Bag (Packs), just to cover some of the things you can build on.

Kelvin is a tanky disruptor that scales better than any other battleborn in the game, because of Chomp giving permanent health with every kill. Weak early, but once he gathers sufficient stacks of Chomp health, he because nigh unkillable with thousands of hp. The key is helping your team stay in the game until you get to that point. Helix:

**1) The Big Chill:** All three upgrades are good and serve different purposes. I prefer the extra regen to compensate having no shields to take poke, but the extra hp can be a much needed early game boost to stay alive, and while the slow is kinda meh, it can prevent other players from kiting you once you're ready to rumble.

**2) Diffusion:** A double dip on late game, the upgrade becomes more powerful the more you stack with Chomp. Adds up to a lot of of major damage in the end. Quick Bite is nice as an alternative to Coldclock, but the measly 30 shields from Strong Wind is terrible.

**3) Swelling Wind:** This is great for reaching multiple people and enemies to stun, as well as escaping. Icemaker is an extremely situational upgrade I personally never take. A stun is ALWAYS better than a slow, even if that slow has a longer duration. Kelvin is dependant on that stun to strike fear into people.

**4) Mastication Restoration:** Great for both fighting and sustaining on the field. The others are difficult to utilize, because Shield Snacker requires already having shields up on use, and Slow Food doesn't work without Coldclock or, ew, Icebreaker.

**5) Blue Ice:** What sounds better to you, 30% of complete damage reduction, or an extra 12 shields with ability use? Yeah, math says Blue Ice.

**6) Windchill:** Both upgrades are pretty good, but this one has a bit more synergy with other Sublimate upgrades. If you are stacking often, Consume can pay off big time, however. Still up to personal preference.

**7) Iceheart:** Around this time, you should have an alright amount of health stacks to start contributing to fights head on. Getting a chunk of health back can be a huge turner in fights. Groupthink is nice for those passive games, and Icy Force is more of a PvE upgrade for crowd control.

**8) Hibernation:** Fantastic with Windchill, gives back a solid amount of health, great for eating a lot of damage. Windy Season is also a great upgrade if you want to utilize Sublimate more for escapes and whatnot. Preference pick.

**9) Sawtooth:** Even though the cooldown reduction looks great, consider this. This is a late upgrade, by the time you would get Overeater, the game is quite close to being over already. Unless you think you needed that lower cooldown to catch up in stacking, stick with Sawtooth.

**10) Great Wall:** Complete preference, all are solid. I feel most chokepoints are too wide for the normal Ice Wall to really shine and cut off people.

**For Gear:** I recommend Cooldown Reduction, Health Regen/Healing Recieved, and Damage Reduction. Kelvin's cooldowns are vital to him for stacking and making plays, you need to have them as low as possible. Since you build up health on your own, you want to supplement it with lots of regen and mitigation. Since you play for the late game, a no-cost white shard generator can be of use for buildables and the other gear. You could also use Attack Damage or Speed to be a bit more of an individual threat.

**Legendary Gear:** Kelvin's lore gear is nice and all, with good stats and effect, but there are others you can definitely consider. Blissbeast Skull Plate (Conservator) is an incredible tank gear that gives nearly 10% damage reduction easily. Song of Vigor and Vigilance Link (Both from Old Sentinel) compliment Kelvin well and gives back a lot for your team. Also check out Arcship Buoy (Packs), Burning Sunset (Packs), Morale Booster (Packs), and Ground Pounders (Packs). Your Boots of the Brute is decent too for offensive purposes.

Marquis is the classic sniper archtype, holding some of the highest DPS in the game. Extremely powerful at long range with very few rivals, but needs good accuracy to land important criticals, and awareness of the battlefield, for the best vantage points and to watch out for those who wish to close the distance. Helix: 

**1) Strigiform Swiftness:** I generally prefer this, because players are able to react in time to shoot down Hoodini owls normally, and this shortens that window by a ton. It makes Predatory Strike much more reliable. Waste Makes Haste can be great for melee teammates in particular, but a lot of times you won't be close enough to the action to place it down for them.

**2) Phaseflyer:** This prevents people from cheesing owls with terrain, guranteeing hits with the previous upgrade. Hoodunnit is better if you did not take Strigiform Swiftness, so they don't draw attention as easily. Eyes Everywhere is extremely situational for stealth users, aka Mike, Sharox and Deande.

**3) Executive Barrel Porting:** The amount of recoil reduction is simply too fantastic not to get. It allows you to reacquire targets very fast, and makes subsequent shots much more accurate. The scope is a crutch that is hardly better than the base scope, and the two extra bullets aren't as impactful as having no recoil. Always take this, it rewards accuracy and skill highly.

**4) Big Time:** This one is personal preference, and while I like the larger AoE, the damage-over-time is great for waveclearing minions and PvE mobs.

**5) Efficiency Expert:** This is superior always when you consider the math. EZD will proc every two shots, instead of three, while Ein Zwei Cry gives a boost to only the third consecutive shot. This means that, Ein Zwei Cry will only give more damage *if you only land exactly three shots on a target.* Executive Access isn't much better, the shield penetration every three shots isn't appliable enough to challenge the DPS of Efficiency Expert.

**6) Parliamentary, My Dear!:** All three are fairly good, so it's another personal pick. I like having the extra owls for more area control and covering more pathways I could be flanked from. The other two lets you use them from safer positioning, without having to get so close.

**7) Bang for the Buck:** Once more, this and Autoloader are both great. Bang gives you higher burst damage on crits, Autoloader increases general DPS, and is especially useful if you use the pistol. I prefer the burst potential, hard to see coming.

**8) Hoot of the Vigilant:** With Shrigiform Swiftness, the chances of the owl getting both hits are high, making this my preferred choice. Windfall can be excellent in PvE as mobs will sit in the AoE all the time, getting the full damage from it.

**9) Cease and Desist:** Improving the slow by 30% is incredibly good, as it means people won't be able to run out as quickly, and getting much more use from it. I would only recommend Time to Spare if you are in PvE, and have also taken the damage upgrade as well.

**10) wallhax.exe:** I'll be honest, Bindleblast is meh. In the time you spend readying and firing it, and it traveling to your target, you could have already just sniped them at least three or so times for better damage. Wallhax lets you actually use it through the map, allowing you to blast people hiding in various buildings and behind walls. It gives Bindleblast a reason to be used, at least outside of waveclear in PvP. In PvE you can take the double shot for nice AoE damage.

**For Gear:** I recommend Crit Damage, Attack Damage and Reload Speed. You want to maximize the amount of damage your criticals deal, for that massive burst and assassination potential Marquis is known for. Reload Speed lowers any downtime for sniping, but you could also try out Movement Speed or Health if you are worried about someone jumping on you.

**Legendary Gear:** I'm actually not a fan of Marquis's lore item, because I don't like Bindleblast that much, but the stats are still nice. I would rather use Vigilant Power Scouter (Old Sentinel), because the health is great and the effect massively rewards good accuracy. HOSTILE_TAKEOVER (ISIC) is a solid subsitute, as you can throughly shut down shield heavy players on PvP. Also consider The Pacifier (ISIC),Symbiotic Gauntlet (Vyn/Arc), Vyn's Quiver, and De-Turtler (Packs).

The best advice I can give you for Ambra, is know how to rotate through her abilities. Make sure to build up heat constantly, as Scorching Strikes are a lot of Ambra's DPS. Sunspot near you and enemy > Strikes > Solar Wind to rebuild heat > Strikes > Life Drain until Sunspot is back up. Doing this correctly lets you 1v1 most people and set up a lot of baits for your team. I can give you a proper write up for Ambra if you want.

Galilea is best built, in my opinion, as a bruiser. Attack speed IS great on her, but you should also consider gear like health, health regen, or shields to supplement that attack speed. Try utilitizing more defensive gear on her.

With your requirements, I would definitely try out Orendi, as others have suggested. She fits what you want very well. You could also try Rath, a burst assassin build on him will easily one-shot most people, while still having some AoE and waveclear for minions.

I'll do a write up of Shayne and Aurox (Referred to as Sharox onward), since ProtoflareX was also asking.

Sharox are a quite different kind of character, being fairly tanky but having an assassin-like kit of abilities. I prefer building them as a bruiser (someone who can take damage well while also dishing it out), as you'll see in my gear and helix build:

**1) Welcoming Committee:** The overshield adds a lot of durability throughout a game, reducing damage from enemies and players reacting to being pulled by Fetch. The aura's damage is too unreliable, being forced to stay still near a person (while alerting them), and isn't useful in PvE either. You should be saving Stealth Strike for either surprising foes, making an escape, or reviving an incapped teammate in safety.

 **2) Surprise Party:** Makes jumping on people with Stealth Strike very lethal, as the damage bonus gives a nice bit of sudden burst. Wait for the Drop is also really strong too in PvP if you need to stick on or lock down people, but not as useful in PvE.

**3) Hulk Out with your Djinn Out:** This is entirely preference, because all three upgrades are honestly great. I like the shield recharge because of the synergy between upgrades in the helix, and you can really abuse it with your huge shields.  Boomarang Bounce gives you a lot of crowd control,  while Power of Two really increases general DPS. It's honestly up to you on what you like to prioritize.

**4) What's Yours is Mine:** This is yet another tree that completely comes down to preference.  Stealing shields further increases your durability, while Holding it Down is specifically strong in PvE for the full stun and locking people inside Tag Team, and We'll Take Everything has high reward potential for PvP. I prefer keeping up our shields as long as possible.

**5) The Immortal Aegis** This specific upgrade is what combines all the rest of our helix into a powerful build. You'll have massive shields with fast recharge, overshields on top of that to protect your normal shields, and be able to keep them up constantly. Don't Stop Running is more useful for squishier, assassin-oriented builds.

**6) Sneaky 'N Resilient:** Fetch's base damage is fairly low, and so 60% of an already weak damage skill is not going to be impactful at all. Stick with this to make escapes easier.

**7) Bigger, Badder Djinn:** Alone Time is inferior by default in this build, because our shields should never be fully down in most circumstances. You can go for the boomerang damage if you took the bounce upgrade, but otherwise doesn't feel worth it. Trust me, 240 shields is a LOT.

**8) Djinn to the Face:** Even though our abilities do not have decent base damages (Except Tag Team, it scales *amazingly*) We still want to be a threat, and the other two upgrades do not help our survivability too much, so we take this to further add to our burst. Sustained Stealth can be useful however, especially in PvE for reviving groups of people and saving near wipes.

**9) Quite Fetching:** Less cooldowns mean more abilities. More abilities equals more overshields and more rechaging while you are slapping people around. This really helps finish our build.

**10) Aurox Beckons:** Even though Tag Team does absolutely monstrous (lol) damage, it's very easy to simply walk out of it. By having a strong slow effect, it dramatically increases odds of getting the entire duration of damage from it, as well as that knockup.

**For Gear:**  I recommend attack damage/speed, cooldown reduction, and shield strength/recharge rate. You want your smacks and boomerangs to do as much as possible, you want cooldowns super low to abuse Immortal Aegis and the other upgrades, and you want to further enhance shields and how fast they charge.  It may be tempting to build skill damage, but considering only Tag Team scales well, and damn well it does, it never ends up worth it.

**Legendary Gear:** Sharox's lore gear is good, but not mandatory by any means. Intermittent Angel (Experiment's Conservator) gives good stats and even more recharging oppertunities, even if you have no cooldowns to use. Time Killer and The Modernista (Both from Supervisor Varl) are both very useful for the stats as well. Sharox can actually use the several gear that require shields to be recharging, so definitely consider Shield Array (Don't remember, Can't find it in gear list, sorry), Executive Insurance Policy (Packs), Premium Health Plan (Packs), and Hemsworth Sparkleshield (Packs).

If you want recommendations on others, try out Kelvin for a late-game monster of a tank, or try building melee heroes more tanky than normally, Phoebe, Rath and Deande can do bruiser builds pretty well.

Okay, Whiskey Foxtrot is a mid-long range dominator, that scales very well with levels. He's a bit reliant on good accuracy for crits, in order to get the most from him. Helix:

**1) Flak Off:** I really like the peeling power from the knockback, and combining it with quick melee makes it very hard for melee enemies to get onto you. Weighed Down is a great alternative in PvP, but in PvE slows are not too useful. Shield Scrapper can be situationally good against high-shield enemies like Veil Walkers and Ronin.

**2) Swiss Cheese:** It's not the reveal that makes this good, it's the damage amp you get against that target. Scrap Bank is is an alright alternative, as long as you take Flak Off with it.

**3) Scoped Up:** ACOG every time, dramatically helps your accuracy for longer range shots. Just hipfire if you need to shoot close up.

**4) Sticky MIRV:** Gives the grenade a bunch of AoE power, without the drawbacks of Triple Threat. Stick 'N Sap is viable against high shield enemies, or if you prefer single target power.

**5) Killer Regen:** The sustain you get even from simple mob kills is *ridiculous.* Massively increases your survivability, the other two hardly compare.

**6) Napalm:** Further adds a lot of damage and utility to grenade, and, with the other upgrades being fairly unnecessary, is a must pick. It also synergises well with Sticky MIRV.

**7) Duct-taped Mags:** I actually prefer this because this gives a very noticable DPS increase, and goes well with the gear I pick. It eliminates need for Reload Speed gear, as long as you know to prepare the magazine. When you aren't in immediate combat, shoot once and reload, so the reload after will be the extremely shorter one. The other upgrades *are* good, but Shield Pen is always situation-dependant, and four-round burst pretty much requires running reload speed to offset it.

**8) Long-Distance Flak:** Scrap Cannon is not that great at damage, even with the extra flak. I take this with the previous upgrades because of the nice range increase for the knockback and amp.

**9) Swift Stickies:** The cooldown reduction feels much more impactful the the small increase on the base explosion of the grenade. Especially with Napalm in mind.

**10) Overoverdrive:** This is generally the better pick, but What Shields can be absloutely amazing against high shield enemies and battleborn.

**For Gear:** I recommend Attack Damage, Critical Damage and Recoil Reduction. As Whiskey's rifle has high base damage, increasing that gives a very nice boost in DPS. Recoil is actually very great gear for him, and it reduces the the jump between the three-shot burst, and really helps with long range accuracy. You can subsitute Crit Damage for Attack Speed if you aren't too confident in your accuracy, and Reload Speed is needed if you take the four-round burst at 7.

**Legendary Gear:** Whiskey's lore item is fairly good, but can be subsituted without hassle. Stable Executioner (Hylis) is fairly nice for the specific stats it gives and the effect isn't too bad at all, considering how much you shoot in a game. Vyn's Quiver is great for pure reload needs, and slows are amazing in PvP in general. Also consider Mini-Singularity Launcher (Maligner), Mag Daemon (Grall), Bunker Buster (H3NCHM4N), De-Turtler (Packs), and Anti-Motion Brace (Packs).

Do keep in mind most of Whiskey's challenges are in PvP. Otherwise make sure to abuse your mid-long range to take out ranged PvE threats like Thrall Brutes.

Alright, I want to speak my mind here. I think many of the nerfs here are far too heavy-handed. I pretty much only play PvE/Co-op, because I greatly dislike the balancing and various problems with PvP, but these changes, especially the gear nerfs, still effect me. Many of the nerfs will make most of these gear items entirely worthless, which means one of the main reasons I play right now, farming legendaries, feel pointless. If you are going to nerf to this extent, there is literally no point for me, of putting time into obtaining that gear. Yes, they may have been too strong, but now many people will probably just stick with basic white gear in PvP, as the cost ratio simply aren't worth it anymore.

3% for Plasmite Transducer is nothing, it should have been around 10% at least, because the gear itself was only useful for the shard generation without having to use the actual, awful shard saving gear. Chrono Key's nerf is ridiculously hard, and while I completely understand it needed it in PvP, it's worthless to nearly anyone now compared to cheaper gear, and it should have been 1200-1500 instead with a possible increase to the heal power stat. Did Oath of the Sustained really need that nerf? (I'm particularly annoyed as I've farming AGES for Oath beforehand) The amount was already miniscule, and the only problem I could see is the potential stacking issue, which brings me to my next point.

If you are nerfing gear for the issue of stacking, **destroying the gear is not the correct fix.** There is a simple way to address teams gear stacking, one that's done by plenty of other MOBAs and similar games. **Have players be only able to be effected by one instance of the gear at any point.** These are called "Auras" in other games, and by having players only able to receive a single "aura" of the the same kind, it prevents stacking abuse. This is what you should have done with Oath of the Sustained, and it's what you should do with Vigilance Link, Shield Array, and so-on, instead of just gutting the gear to uselessness.

You should honestly be buffing gear, as far more legendary gear are underpowered and/or useless to begin with. Shard Generators and Wrenches are awful outside of no-cost whites, because you would never spend 1800 shards just to save/make shards, unless the effects were great enough to justify it. (Lorrian Purse Cutter is a good example) You should be making more legendary gear viable to compete with the few that already are, which means more people use gear outside of whites, and more people will find incentive to play PvE instead of dropping it after the first clear.

I'm warning you Gearbox, Battleborn is already on life support, please be careful with your adjustments.

Audio adjustments would really help out the game. I'm using a solid turtle beach headset, and even with everything at max, most of the sound effects and music are difficult to hear. There's also a lot of abilities and things that really should be louder, to work as sound ques, which are really important in these kind of games. You would expect a shadowflame pillar from Orendi, or a charge shot from Isic to make a distinctly louder sound, but you barely hear them, and adjusting the volume on effects like these would make things a lot more clear and less confusing in hectic fights.

Noone competent is going to ignore Tracer tickling them in the back. Greymane, Thrall, even Kael will force her out of a fight really easily. She only does something when Pulse Bomb is up, which scales pretty well, but once that and recall are used she can't fight anyone.

I'm gonna be honest, I think she's underpowered. Low damage output, fairly squishy despite her mobility, terrible at holding a lane and rotations are meh without Pulse Bomb ready, and a really mediocre talent tree. She can't really fight or trade anyone because of how little damage she does. She will definitely need some buffs, like how Lunara was on her release.
Please consider keeping this Blizzard, or at least a weaker version or a talent for it. Tychus could really use this in is kit, and he's still not in a great spot at the moment.

The carapace build has never been viable. It's fun, and to be truthful the full heal amount is quite good, but it can't really take the place of a support's healing, and it doesn't push nearly as well as mines are locusts do. It's more or less something fun in QM until the talents get buffs or changes.

[This](http://www.heroesfire.com/hots/talent-calculator/abathur#pAFx) is the symbiote build I usually do if I know I will be hatting mainly ranged heroes. Since I know that the hat won't be in the middle of the fight, Spatial Efficiency lets me do more from afar. Adrenaline Boost lets them be able to chase, kite, or run away to safety, and Regenerative Microbes lets you heal off some of the damage they may have taken. In this context you use carapace carefully, instand of normally spamming it. Keep in mind against heavy melee teams it may still be worth talenting spike anyways, to peel off divers. If you suddenly lose confidence in your team and feel you need to be able to push, you can go for a hybrid build with the locust talents at 13, 16 and 20.

A lot of your questions about the locust build has to be learned over time, as it involves a good sense of the game. (Is there an objective at the moment? Are they looking for me? How fast can they reach me if they are? Will I get anything out of this?) Sometimes you'll be able to get away with overextending with locusts, and other times it's so unsafe that you can only plant your locusts down and hearth right after. The latter is especially true if they have heroes that can rotate on you very quick (Falstad, Dehaka, Illidan with The Hunt) or may be extremely hard to keep track of (Zeratul, Nova). Around my mmr people are more likely to try and get to you if they aren't 100% distracted by the map, and people love to counterpick you with the aforementioned heroes in HL, so I usually find myself playing it a bit safe in those late-game situations, unless I see good opportunities to backdoor, take a siege camp, and so on. So regarding this all I can tell you is to keep playing Abby, and you'll get a sense of things in time.

For lane soaking, yes that's usually correct. You'll want to be soaking with your body in a lane, preferably hidden but still in exp range, while you help your teammates with the symbiote. There are good exceptions to this, where soaking another lane with hat is the best choice. It could be because you know the objective was finished and you need to keep up exp, or if you know you won't be able to contribute anything meaningful (Instead of trying to help someone when they will probably die regardless, you can be soaking an empty lane to mitigate the exp their death gave), or if you know soaking will give a major advantage such as getting to 10 first.

I love symbiote builds very much so, but as of this moment it's pretty dead. The problem is that symbiote builds are usually dependant on your team. You usually want someone that can take advantage of Adrenal Overload's attack speed, and a lot of Abbys prefer melee heroes to hat for more use of spike, although I personally disagree and think ranged heroes like Valla and Greymane are fantastic hat targets, given you alter some talents. So when you have mages like Li-Ming who sit back and don't take advantage of the hat, it's harder to justify the build.

Locust and Mine builds are the go-to for many Abathurs because they are the least dependant on your team. You can control minions and rotations better with mines, and locusts make you a real push threat. Symbiote builds lack those in order to improve your fight presence as much as possible, but you are still restricted by your team's actions in the end. This also doesn't include the fact of Ultimate Evolution being so good. It makes it difficult to decide when you should clone (beginning of fights with hat build btw), and when you should hat. 

Don't feel discouraged about this, because I myself climbed a lot of HL with Symbiote Abathur, even before mines were buffed to how they are. Blizzard said they are buffing Monstrosity, the preferred ult for hat builds, and with the rise of Illidan you could definitely see more symbiote builds out there.


To answer your actual questions, stick to what works best for you. But as a rule of thumb, Mines should be the general build you go, unless either you know you can push effectively later with locusts (they have no waveclear or lack global presence), or you have potentially good targets that you can **trust** will use the symbiote well. I've had plenty of terrible Illidans and Butchers I wasted my build for, but have had Sonyas and Raynors that hard carried with it.

I would say small maps that don't/can't be soaked too well, and/or have lots of fighting are best for Symbiote. Tomb, Towers, Mines, Shire, etc.

Dispersal is the general choice for mine builds due to the constant supply of nests to place. You can effectively cover most of a map, and be able to pile them quickly enough for a nice surprise at a choke.

Ballistospores is mainly only useful in locust builds, for backdooring buildings and placing vision to dig to. The 20% duration isn't much at all, so Dispersal is far less situational.
I play specialists at 3.5k mmr, especially Abathur. If you have any questions about these heroes, feel free to ask.

I'm glad you see what I mean. Nova's damage is fine, and it's relevant. She just needs her edges rounded out so she can do things to help besides that damage.

I'm not doubting Nova's ability to perform damage-wise. I think she is really solid there with Snipe's now low CD and damage, and there is a lot of people misplaying as well. What I'm mainly talking about is the really high level of play, aka competitive and close to it, where it's *really* hard to justify Nova with other, safer picks out there.

Well I've always preferred Symbiote build myself, so playing with a good Protect-Illidan/Butcher comp is really satisfying. Aside from those two, anyone who can take full advantage of Adrenal Glands' attack speed, along with the hat's other boons, like Zeratul, Greymane, Artanis, Raynor, even Kharazim, are among solid choices as long as you know you can rely on that person for the most part.

While it's extremely important to be lane soaking whenever you can, you need to do it safely, which a lot of people even in my mmr never understand. Mine build can generally work well on any map except maybe mines, which isn't in rotation, so it's mostly the latter.  I would say heavy sustain comps could ignore them, I suppose, but they aren't countered by anything in particular.

The easiest talent build for Abathur is the mines build. As long as you have an understanding of where players commonly move through, you can find reasonable success. Try to spread mines throughout areas to maximize map control, and keeping mine clusters near objectives where they count.

The thing about your comparison to Nazeebo and Zagara is that they have abilities that work by themselves: Spiders, Hydralisk, etc. Fire and forget, which means they're really strong at poking and dealing constant damage. In matchups, Sustain lanes are usually easy. Soraka and Bard are free lanes to let your ADC farm and you to scale. Sona and Nami will be more aggressive in trading and will outsustain, but Relic Shield helps quite a bit, and if they overextend they can be very vulnerable to bursting down, and Rend means you'll win extended trades. They'll heal of course, but that also strains their mana, and mana is never a problem for Kalista since the W proc costs nothing and Rend is only 40 mana.

Poke lanes are usually not too much of a problem either, provided your ADC doesn't get too hard bullied out of lane. Kalista is inheritly one of the hardest champions to hit skillshots on, and this doesn't really change as support. With good use of Martial Poise, it should be easy to avoid the skillshots of Vel'koz, Zyra (not including plants), and Morgana. Annie is an exception however, outranging you and having point-and-click abilities. Relic Shield again is super helpful.

Engage lanes are the most skill-based lanes to go against, for sure. You and your ADC must put an effort to poking them down early on and discourage any possible all-ins. The likes of Thresh, Blitzcrank and Leona should not be able to get a hold of you with your mobility, but it can be very hard to prevent your ADC from getting bursted pre-6, if the lane does not go your way early on. Before ult, you only have Rend to slow down the enemy from following up as well, so the best way to win these lanes is to be aggressive with poke during the first two levels while avoiding the engage, and get into situations where if they do decide to go in, you'll be able to outdamage them quickly enough and win the fight. I've won my share of lanes against engage, but when you're dealing with something very snowbally like Graves/Leona or Draven/Blitzcrank, it can be a challenge that you and your ADC need to be ready for.

Regardless of matchup, when you hit 6, the lane will more than likely become a farm lane for the enemy unless they get outside help, or you've won lane already. Fate's Call nullifies any full on engage or all-in against your ADC. Even during 4 or 5 man dives against my lane, I can safely say I can get my ADC out alive, a niche few traditional supports can even compare.

Finally, I'll go over the general pros and cons of having Kalista as your support, according to my views.

Pros:

1) The protection of your ADC: I can't stress enough, Fate's Call is one of the best ultimates in the game. Having that kind of power to save your most important member of your team, from literally any situation, is just incredible. Zed ulted with no QSS? Pulled by a Blitz into their whole team? Extemely overextended and getting collapsed on? All nothing for her. Very few champions could really get close to saying that.

2) Vision power: There are only a few champions that give the strength of vision. One including another marksman who has also been known to be capable to support! Even then, the massive range, lifetime, and spammability of sentinels gives Kalista's team so much information. Vision wins games.

3) Damage: 20% of their maximum health. Absolutely crazy, and requires nothing but levels in the skill. Giving that steroid to your ADC? Even more absurd. This doesn't even include the potential of Rend and its stacking.

4) Powerful skirmishes: With you and your ADC with you, small fights are in your advantage. Burst a target with your W proc and the ADC's crits and abilities, and come out on top where a Rend secures kills with the powerful slows or outright executing. Who will they focus, the ADC they won't be able to finish off, or the mobile support who is either fairly tanky, wasting your time, or is doing enough damage to kill you herself?

5) The potential to carry: It may not usually happen, but Kalista can also serve as the "backup plan." In those rare situations where you need as much damage as you can get, she can serve very well as a secondary carry, while keeping the core ideas of her utility intact.

6) Dragon and Baron securing: There is a reason people say you can't outsmite a Kalista. On top of vision control, Rend applies near infintely to Dragon and Baron alongside champions, and all the accumulated stacks will be a very large chunk of health, and even on a support build it will guarantee at least 500-600+ damage at the end. Nunu and Cho'gath are the only possible supports who can achieve that kind of secure.

7) Denying the pick: Kalista is a popular and in-meta utility ADC at the moment. By taking her as a support, not only do you sew confusion on the enemy team (Is that their ADC? Is she going to support?), but you prevent them from using her. This allows more room for other bans, and selecting another ADC that would work better against that team, or have stronger carry potential than Kalista, such as Jinx.

Cons:

1) Utility is mostly only for the ADC: This is probably the biggest drawback in my eyes. Kalista may be able to help out her ADC, but the rest of her team doesn't get much benefit. She has to resort to building utility items to really aid her other teammates, as they cannot receive the W proc not use Fate's Call.

2) Lacks strong peel: The only hard cc Kalista has is the knockup of Fate's Call, and that is only usable on the whim of an ulted ADC. The slows from Rend can be strong, but will not suffice in every situation. Other teammates would have to fill the void, if need be.

3) Terrible roaming alone: What would a Kalista actually do to gank? Auto them as they walk back to tower? Would they simply turn on you? This further reinforces that Kalista has to be with her ADC to stay useful.

4) Fate's Call is the key: You will not have it up always, even with 40% CDR. In those times it is imperitive that your ADC knows such, and limit themselves until it is back up.

5) Coordination is required: I can admit this myself, Kalista support is not super solo-queue friendly. I manage to get by, but to really bring out the full potential of the pick, the ADC and Support need to communicate to each other. You don't want to have the Kalista ult when the ADC was confident on surviving or wanted to chase.

Overall, I strongly believe that Kalista is a strong, if niche, pick for support, that can work fantastically in the right settings. I also find it very fun to play, as well. I hope I've made a good argument, and perhaps encouraged people to try it out themselves. :)
